slices.focus: After a friend notices her looking drawn on a ferry, Ayaka finally visits a clinic for anti-nausea and sleep advice, shifting from endurance to management.
slices.summary: Nozomi sees Ayaka looking ill on a ferry and pushes her to visit a clinic. The doctor confirms the nausea-sleep-stress cycle is real and gives practical advice: time anti-nausea medicine earlier, eat bland food before crossings, and stop trying to force sleep. Ayaka starts being more selective about unnecessary island crossings during typhoon weeks and builds a short pre-sleep routine.
open_loops: New routines may not survive peak typhoon pressure
Guilt about reducing island visits may resurface
Nausea management is palliative, not structural — rough crossings remain unavoidable
